target.title: fix(mac): opening General Settings crashes in packaged app
target.body:
Closes #111270

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening General Settings in the packaged macOS 2026.7.2 app would immediately crash when the Quick Chat shortcut recorder rendered.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hand-built macOS app did not include KeyboardShortcuts' generated SwiftPM resource bundle, while the dependency's default bundle lookup assumes that resource exists. The package step now patches the dependency to prefer the app-packaged resource bundle, copies that bundle into the app with a fail-closed check, and preserves the committed Swift package resolution byte-for-byte across resolve and build commands.

The regression coverage exercises both the package script boundary and the hosted General Settings view so a successful Swift compile alone cannot mask a broken distributable app.

## User Impact

Users can open General Settings and use the Quick Chat shortcut recorder without the macOS app terminating.

Release note: Fix macOS General Settings crashing when the Quick Chat shortcut recorder loads from a packaged app.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the 2026.7.2 failure as a main-thread `NSBundle.module` assertion from `KeyboardShortcuts.RecorderCocoa.configureView`; the installed bundle inventory lacked `KeyboardShortcuts_KeyboardShortcuts.bundle`.
- Focused package tests: 26 passed, 2 platform skips (28 total).
- Blacksmith changed gate: passed, including formatting, dependency/patch guards, root test typechecking, script lint, and the macOS packaging lane (57 passed, 13 platform skips in the surrounding tooling/daemon shards).
- Built the exact head `28f7ca57264af411b56f6f923dd9e48ede387835` as a packaged macOS app, signed it with Developer ID team `Y5PE65HELJ`, and passed `codesign --verify --deep --strict`. The app embedded the exact commit and contained the KeyboardShortcuts English localization bundle.
- Native accessibility proof opened `OpenClaw Settings`, rendered `General`, `Quick Chat`, the configured `⌥Space` recorder, and the localized empty-state `Record Shortcut` field. A source-blind validator confirmed the exact packaged process remained alive through a fresh 16-second observation window in both recorder states.
- Fresh autoreview found no accepted or actionable findings.

AI-assisted: Codex was used for diagnosis, implementation, tests, and validation; the maintainer reviewed the code and understands the change.
